tldr: AVALONBENCH is a benchmark introducing a comprehensive game environment for evaluating multi-agent LLMs playing the strategic social deduction game Resistance Avalon, revealing a significant capability gap between current LLM agents and rule-based baseline bots.
contributions: Introduction of AVALONBENCH, a benchmark based on Resistance Avalon for studying multi-agent game playing of LLM agents
A game environment that records all players' actions and progresses the game
Naive AI bots with deterministic rule-based strategies serving as baselines
Baseline implementations of ReAct-style LLM agents with carefully designed prompts
Demonstration that current LLM agents lack deduction, persuasion, negotiation, and deception capabilities needed to play Avalon well
methods: The authors built AVALONBENCH, a game engine for the hidden-identity social deduction game Resistance Avalon. They implemented ReAct-style LLM agents (using GPT-3.5-turbo and Llama2-7B) that generate actions, dialogue, and game history summaries through structured prompts. The pipeline uses a Reason-then-Action paradigm where LLMs receive game rules, role information, summaries, discussion minutes, and action requests, with a separate parser converting outputs into game-readable format. They also implemented four naive rule-based bots (Naive Servant, Naive Minion, Naive Assassin, Naive Merlin) that use only mission outcomes without considering voting or dialogue history.
results: ChatGPT playing good-role achieved a win rate of 22.2% against rule-based bots playing evil, while the good-role rule-based bot achieved 38.2% win rate in the same setting. For evil-role, LLM agents achieved 66.7% win rate compared to 61.8% for the rule-based evil bot. These results demonstrate a clear capability gap, with LLMs failing against even simple baseline players.
limitations: Current LLM agents lack deduction, persuasion, negotiation, and deception capabilities required for Avalon
LLMs fail against even the simplest rule-based baseline players
Longer context may confine the ability of LLMs to reason and parse through noise
The Naive Merlin reveals its identity easily through voting patterns
The paper notes future plans to add voting randomness to the Naive Merlin baseline
